s0101.literal: With steadfast purpose he loved learning, especially excelled at documents and records, and was known for talent and arts.
s0101.idiomatic: He was steadfast in study, especially skilled at documents and records, and won renown for talent and literary craft.

s0102.literal: On leaving the black lacquered cap he was made Left Regular Attendant of the Liang Prince of Nanping's kingdom, Acting Retainer of the Prince of Hedong's light-chariot establishment, and concurrently Master of Writing; soon he was made regular.
s0102.idiomatic: He began his career as left regular attendant in the Prince of Nanping's kingdom, acting retainer in the Prince of Hedong's light-chariot staff, and concurrent master of writing; soon he held the post in full.

s0103.literal: He went out as magistrate of Anji, was moved to out-of-quota recorder in the Prince of Shaoling's eastern establishment, and concurrently magistrate of Jiankang.
s0103.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Anji, then became out-of-quota recorder to the Prince of Shaoling and concurrent magistrate of Jiankang.

s0104.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, Emperor Wen and Chi had an old acquaintance, Editorial footnote marker 11. and when Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wu Xing, he made Chi assistant administrator of the commandery and put him in charge of documents; from then on Chi regularly relied on Emperor Wen.
s0104.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, Emperor Wen and Chi were old acquaintances [11]. When Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Xing, he made Chi assistant administrator and put him in charge of documents; from then on Chi always followed Emperor Wen.

s0105.literal: When Emperor Wen overcame Zhang Biao and garrisoned Kuaiji, he again had Chi oversee Linhai commandery.
s0105.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen defeated Zhang Biao and garrisoned Kuaiji, he again had Chi oversee Linhai commandery.

s0106.literal: Because of greedy license he lost the people's goodwill; mountain bandits seized him and held him in secret for a hundred days; Emperor Wen sent Liu Cheng to suppress them and pacify the region, and only then was Chi released.
s0106.idiomatic: Through greedy excess he lost popular support; mountain bandits seized and held him in secret for a hundred days. Emperor Wen sent Liu Cheng to suppress them, and Chi was only then released.

s0107.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Chi was appointed Adviser to the Pacifying-East Prince of Linchuan's establishment.
s0107.idiomatic: When the Founder received the Mandate, Chi was made adviser to the pacifying-east Prince of Linchuan's establishment.

s0108.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was moved to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
s0108.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng (560) he was promoted to left assistant director of the masters of writing.

s0109.literal: For merit in the Changcheng campaign he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chongde, fief three hundred households.
s0109.idiomatic: For merit at Changcheng he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chongde, with a fief of three hundred households.

s0110.literal: On the day of enfeoffment he asked a clerical officer to be his guest and accepted his gifts; Emperor Wen was angry and had him dismissed on that account.
s0110.idiomatic: On the day he received his fief he entertained a clerical officer as guest and accepted his gifts; Emperor Wen was furious and dismissed him for it.

s0111.literal: Soon he was made Adviser to the Propagating-Favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.
s0111.idiomatic: Soon he was made adviser to the propagating-favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.

s0112.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an; for beating a county commoner to death he lost his enfeoffment.
s0112.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an; for beating a county commoner to death he lost his fief.

s0115.literal: Collation variant: (huan). He was made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
s0115.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

s0116.literal: Editorial footnote marker 13. He was made General of Edge Glory and magistrate of Yanguan.
s0116.idiomatic: [13] He was made General of Edge Glory and magistrate of Yanguan.

s0117.literal: In the first year of Guangda he was moved to Director of the Secretariat and put in charge of national history.
s0117.idiomatic: In Guangda year 1 (567) he was made director of the secretariat and put in charge of the national history.

s0118.literal: He was again made Director of the Palace Storehouses and concurrently supervised the Feathered Forest.
s0118.idiomatic: He was again made director of the palace storehouses and concurrently supervised the Feathered Forest guard.

s0119.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers.
s0119.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of palace affairs and concurrently colonel of footsoldiers.

s0120.literal: In the first year of Taijian he died, aged sixty-two.
s0120.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he died, aged sixty-two.

s0121.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
s0121.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

s0122.literal: Chi was skilled at calligraphy; whenever he composed, he liked to use unusual characters, and men of letters also ridiculed him for this.
s0122.idiomatic: Chi was skilled at calligraphy; whenever he wrote, he favored odd characters, and literary men mocked him for it.

s0123.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
s0123.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten juan.

s0124.literal: Xu Heng, styled Hendao, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang—sixth-generation descendant of the Jin Recluse Xu Xun.
s0124.idiomatic: Xu Heng, styled Hendao, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang, sixth-generation descendant of the Jin recluse Xu Xun.

s0125.literal: His great-grandfather Gui served as Attendant, was appointed Administrator of Guiyang, but honored his will and lived on Mount Jiu in Yongxing—the very place Xun had hidden.
s0125.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui had been an attendant and was appointed administrator of Guiyang, but honored his own resolve and lived on Mount Jiu in Yongxing—the very retreat of Xu Xun.

s0126.literal: His grandfather Yonghui was Liang Household Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Supernumerary Vice Director of the Masters of Writing for the Heir Apparent.
s0126.idiomatic: His grandfather Yonghui had been Liang household tutor to the heir apparent and supernumerary vice director of the masters of writing for the heir apparent.

s0127.literal: His father Mao was Liang Administrator of the two commanderies of Shiping and Tianmen, Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he was known for learning and arts and compiled Meaning and Categories of the Mao Odes' Winds, Elegies, and Hymns in fifteen juan and Records of Conduct in four juan.
s0127.idiomatic: His father Mao had been Liang administrator of Shiping and Tianmen, junior mentor to the heir apparent, and scattered-cavalry regular attendant; known for learning and the arts, he compiled Meaning and Categories of the Mao Odes' Winds, Elegies, and Hymns in fifteen juan and Records of Conduct in four juan.

s0128.literal: Heng in youth transmitted the family profession; solitary and upright, he had integrity in conduct.
s0128.idiomatic: Heng in youth carried on the family learning; solitary and upright, he was known for integrity.

s0129.literal: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of former-age antiquities; elders of reputation all commended him, and the Nanyang Liu Zhibian especially valued him and often praised him to others.
s0129.idiomatic: He mastered all books and knew former ages well; men of standing commended him, and Liu Zhibian of Nanyang especially prized him and often spoke of him.

s0130.literal: On leaving the black lacquered cap he was made Acting Retainer in the Prince of An Dong's establishment, Editorial footnote marker 14. concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University; soon he was made Recorder of the Pacifying-West establishment.
s0130.idiomatic: He began as acting retainer in the Prince of An Dong's establishment [14], concurrently erudite of the imperial university; soon he became recorder of the pacifying-west establishment.

s0131.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he was Central Recorder of the Pacifying-West Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
s0131.idiomatic: At the start of Taiqing (547) he was central recorder of the pacifying-west army and concurrently vice director of the imperial ancestral temple.

s0132.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Yingzhou; when the Liang Prince of Shaoling came by the eastern route, Heng was recruited as Adviser.
s0132.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Yingzhou; when the Liang Prince of Shaoling came by the eastern route, Heng was recruited as adviser.

s0133.literal: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou, having long heard his name, he summoned Heng as Acting Retainer of the Masters of Writing with the same powers as a full one.
s0133.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou he had long heard of Heng and summoned him as acting retainer of the masters of writing with full powers.

s0134.literal: He was moved to Retainer of the Masters of Writing to the Grand Marshal and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed documents; court and government affairs were wholly entrusted to them.
s0134.idiomatic: He was promoted to retainer of the masters of writing to the grand marshal and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed documents; all court and government business was entrusted to them.

s0135.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an assumed the regency, Heng was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate; Heng submitted a memorial declining the staff post, and Sengbian replied: "Your report is received; I learn you have received a court appointment—a fine selection of virtue.
s0135.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin'an assumed the regency, Heng was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate; Heng submitted a memorial declining the staff post. Sengbian replied, "Your report is received; I learn you have a court appointment—a fine choice of virtue.

s0136.literal: Your conduct is sincere and deep, your literary arts comprehensive; learning excellence fitting office—you would reach the purple ranks yourself.
s0136.idiomatic: Your conduct is sincere and deep and your literary arts comprehensive; with learning fit for office you would reach the purple ranks on your own.

s0137.literal: Moreover long constrained, a swift horse about to be halted; to aid and correct in a vacant and dim hour, the hope placed in you is truly deep.
s0137.idiomatic: Moreover you have long been constrained, a swift horse about to be reined in; to aid and correct in this vacant and dim hour, the hope placed in you is truly deep.

s0138.literal: Though glad you may roam freely and forget weariness, yet the thorn bush harboring a feng-bird—this always adds to my sighs.
s0138.idiomatic: Though I am glad you may go freely and forget hardship, a feng-bird nesting in thorn bushes always adds to my sighs.

s0139.literal: The choice of 'evening gentleman' is though clear and eminent; the post is risen to by talent—you need scarcely feel shame.
s0139.idiomatic: The post of Gentleman of the Evening, though clear and eminent, is won by talent—you need feel little shame.

s0140.literal: Moreover you first said you knew your fate, were just racing on the broad way, had not yet the weariness of bearing halberds, yet already the grief of night travel—reading your letter again, I am quite disquieted.
s0140.idiomatic: Moreover you first said you knew your fate and were racing along the broad road, had not yet the weariness of bearing halberds, yet already grieve at night travel—reading your letter again, I am deeply troubled.

s0141.literal: Ancients in mutual longing would drive a thousand li; a pure heart is not obscured—how could city walls limit it? The depth of care you show leaves me endlessly ashamed."
s0141.idiomatic: Ancients in longing would drive a thousand li; a pure heart is not dimmed—how could city walls limit it? The depth of your regard leaves me endlessly ashamed."

s0142.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Heng was appointed Grand Master of the Palace and supervised the Feathered Forest.
s0142.idiomatic: When the Founder received the Mandate, Heng was made grand master of the palace and supervised the Feathered Forest guard.

s0143.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and concurrently Grand Historiographer, in charge of Liang history.
s0143.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of palace affairs and concurrently grand historiographer, in charge of Liang history.

s0144.literal: At first, when Sengbian was put to death, the responsible office seized Sengbian and his son Yan's Collation variant: (shi). corpse, Editorial footnote marker 15. and buried them together in one pit at Mount Fang; by this time none dared speak of it.
s0144.idiomatic: When Sengbian was executed, the authorities seized him and his son Yan's corpse [15] and buried them together in one pit at Mount Fang; by then none dared speak of it.

s0145.literal: Heng as a former clerk submitted a memorial requesting burial; then with his old comrades Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others, they jointly used family wealth to prepare the funeral
s0145.idiomatic: Heng, as a former clerk, submitted a memorial requesting burial; then he and his old comrades Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others jointly used family wealth to prepare the funeral

s0147.literal: , Editorial footnote marker 16. all seven coffins were reburied.

s0148.literal: He had first compiled the Qi History with treatises in fifty juan, but it was lost in the turmoil.
s0148.idiomatic: He had first compiled the Qi History with treatises in fifty juan, but it was lost in the chaos.

s0149.literal: Later he compiled the Liang History; what was completed came to fifty-eight juan.
s0149.idiomatic: Later he compiled the Liang History; the completed portion ran to fifty-eight juan.

s0150.literal: Literary writings composed after Liang's Taiqing period, six juan.
s0150.idiomatic: Literary writings composed after Liang's Taiqing period, six juan.

s0151.literal: His son Shansin was known early and reached the post of Vice Director of Revenue in the Masters of Writing.
s0151.idiomatic: His son Shansin was known from youth and rose to vice director of revenue in the masters of writing.

s0152.literal: Chu Yu, styled Wenli, was a native of Yangzhai in Henan.
s0152.idiomatic: Chu Yu, styled Wenli, came from Yangzhai in Henan.

s0153.literal: His great-grandfather Xuan, at the beginning of Song's Shengming era, entered attendance in the palace hall with Xie Tiao, Jiang Xiao, and Liu Yi and were called the Four Friends.
s0153.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xuan, at the start of Song's Shengming era, attended in the palace hall with Xie Tiao, Jiang Xiao, and Liu Yi and were called the Four Friends.

s0154.literal: He reached Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title Viscount of Zhen.
s0154.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing, with posthumous title Viscount of Zhen.

s0155.literal: His grandfather Yun was Liang Imperial Censor.
s0155.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun was Liang imperial censor.

s0156.literal: His father Meng was Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
s0156.idiomatic: His father Meng was attendant to the heir apparent.

s0157.literal: Yu was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, Acting Retainer of the Masters of Writing to the Flying Cavalry General.
s0157.idiomatic: Yu was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, acting retainer of the masters of writing to the flying-cavalry general.

s0158.literal: From early on he had a fine reputation; elders for the most part commended his talent and capacity.
s0158.idiomatic: From youth he had a fine reputation; elders mostly commended his talent and capacity.

s0159.literal: When he grew up he had fine bearing, was skilled at repartee, broadly learned and able to compose, his phrasing classical and solid, and did not like florid excess.
s0159.idiomatic: As he matured he had fine bearing, was skilled at repartee, broadly learned and able to compose; his style was classical and solid, without florid excess.

s0160.literal: He began his career as Legal Officer of a princely establishment and through transfers became Outer Army Recorder.
s0160.idiomatic: He began as legal officer of a princely establishment and through transfers became outer-army recorder.

s0161.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was concurrently Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access, was sent as envoy to Qi, and on return became Friend to the Prince of Guiyang.
s0161.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was concurrently regular attendant of unimpeded access, was envoy to Qi, and on return became friend to the Prince of Guiyang.

s0162.literal: He was moved to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Master of Writing Attendant.
s0162.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior mentor to the heir apparent and master of writing attendant.

s0163.literal: In the Taijian era Shanyin county had many powerful ruffians; successive magistrates were all dismissed for bribery and corruption; Emperor Gaozong was troubled by this and said to Master of Writing Attendant Cai Jingli: "Ji Yin is a great county and long without a good magistrate; among men of letters, try to think of someone.
s0163.idiomatic: In the Taijian era Shanyin county had many powerful ruffians and successive magistrates were dismissed for bribery; Emperor Gaozong was troubled and told master of writing attendant Cai Jingli, "Shanyin is a great county long without a good magistrate; among literary men, think of someone."

s0164.literal: " Jingli advanced and said: "Chu Yu is frugal and has practical ability—would he be unknown to be fit for the selection?
s0164.idiomatic: " Jingli replied, "Chu Yu is frugal and capable—would he be unknown whether he fits the post?"

s0165.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Very good—your words match my intent.
s0165.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "Excellent—your words match my intent."

s0166.literal: " He was then made General of Military Glory and magistrate of Shanyin.
s0166.idiomatic: Yu was then made General of Military Glory and magistrate of Shanyin.

s0167.literal: County commoners Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and others bribed and colluded with crafty clerks; whole-household great families for the most part concealed their registers.
s0167.idiomatic: County commoners Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and others bribed crafty clerks; great households for the most part concealed their registers.

s0168.literal: Yu then locked up Cide and the rest, submitted a full report to the capital, and Emperor Gaozong personally wrote in consolation and reward and also sent envoys to help Yu search and register; more than eight hundred military and civilian households were brought out.
s0168.idiomatic: Yu then imprisoned Cide and the rest and submitted a full report to the capital; Emperor Gaozong personally wrote to console and reward him and sent envoys to help Yu search the registers, exposing more than eight hundred military and civilian households.

s0169.literal: At the time Attendant Cao Yida was favored by Emperor Gaozong; county commoner Chen Xin was rich in wealth and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on influence and acted violently.
s0169.idiomatic: Attendant Cao Yida was then favored by Emperor Gaozong; county commoner Chen Xin was wealthy and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on power and acted violently.

s0170.literal: Yu then sent officers to seize Xianwen and gave him a hundred strokes of the whip; from then on clerks and people trembled and none dared offend.
s0170.idiomatic: Yu then sent officers to seize Xianwen and gave him a hundred strokes of the whip; thereafter clerks and people trembled and none dared offend.

s0171.literal: Later Xin, through Yida, slandered Yu, and in the end Yu was dismissed from office on that account.
s0171.idiomatic: Later Xin slandered Yu through Yida, and Yu was dismissed.

s0172.literal: Yu in office for more than a year kept only his salary; on the day he left office he could not support himself on the journey and therefore remained within the county border, planting vegetables to support himself.
s0172.idiomatic: Yu held office for more than a year and kept only his salary; when he left he could not afford the journey and stayed within the county, planting vegetables to live.

s0173.literal: Some mocked Yu as lacking the talent of a hundred-li magistrate; Yu replied: "My delivery of taxes and ranking among commanderies is not behind other cities; in removing the violent and ridding the cruel, crafty clerks cowered.
s0173.idiomatic: Some mocked Yu as unfit for a county magistrate; Yu replied, "My tax deliveries and rankings are not behind other cities; in removing violence and ridding cruelty, crafty clerks cowered.

s0174.literal: If you mean I could not enrich myself with grease and ointment, that is as fate ordained.
s0174.idiomatic: If you mean I could not enrich myself with bribes, that is as fate ordained.

s0175.literal: To say I did not understand governing—I am not convinced.
s0175.idiomatic: To say I did not understand governing—I am not convinced.

s0176.literal: Men of the time held this credible.
s0176.idiomatic: Men of the time found this credible.

s0177.literal: The Heir Apparent knew Yu had no travel funds; he personally wrote and granted two hundred piculs of grain and millet, and Yu then returned to the capital.
s0177.idiomatic: The heir apparent knew Yu had no travel funds and personally wrote to grant him two hundred piculs of grain and millet; Yu then returned to the capital.

s0178.literal: The Heir Apparent loved Yu's literary compositions and had him enter attendance in the Hall Directorate.
s0178.idiomatic: The heir apparent admired Yu's writing and had him attend in the hall directorate.

s0179.literal: In the tenth year he was made General of Lightning Might and Long Recorder to the Prince of Huainan of Renwei; soon he held his former post and concurrently managed Eastern Palace records.
s0179.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made General of Lightning Might and long recorder to the Prince of Huainan of Renwei; soon he held the same rank and concurrently managed eastern-palace records.

s0180.literal: In the twelfth year he was moved to Imperial Censor and died in office, aged fifty-two.
s0180.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made imperial censor and died in office, aged fifty-two.

s0181.literal: Yu was resolute and had bold decision; he was also skilled at mounted archery.
s0181.idiomatic: Yu was resolute and bold in decision; he was also skilled at mounted archery.

s0182.literal: Once he followed Minister of Works Hou Andu on a hunt at Xuzhou; they encountered a fierce beast, Editorial footnote marker 17. Yu drew his bow and shot; twice he hit the mouth entering the belly, and soon the beast fell dead.
s0182.idiomatic: Once he followed Minister of Works Hou Andu hunting at Xuzhou; they met a fierce beast [17]. Yu drew his bow and shot twice, both entering the mouth into the belly, and the beast soon fell dead.

s0183.literal: When he was Imperial Censor he had a great reputation for the straight cord.
s0183.idiomatic: As imperial censor he won a great reputation for upholding the law.

s0184.literal: From the end of Liang's turmoil court regulations were abandoned and neglected; the judicial office followed precedent, kept them and did not reform; Yu was just about to change and expand them, making great regulations and broadly setting out the net, but the compilation was not finished, and therefore they are not listed in what follows.
s0184.idiomatic: From Liang's final turmoil court regulations had collapsed; the judicial office clung to precedent without reform. Yu was about to overhaul them with broad new regulations, but the compilation was unfinished, and therefore they are not listed below.

s0185.literal: When he died the Heir Apparent personally composed his epitaph to show remembrance of old ties.
s0185.idiomatic: When he died the heir apparent personally composed his epitaph in remembrance of old ties.

s0186.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.
s0186.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 (584) he was posthumously made director of the secretariat.

s0187.literal: Memorials and miscellaneous writings he composed, more than two hundred pieces, all hit the facts of affairs, and on this account he was valued in his time.
s0187.idiomatic: More than two hundred memorials and essays he wrote all addressed the facts of affairs, and on that account he was valued in his time.

s0188.literal: His son Liang had talent and learning and reached Attendant in the Hall Directorate of the Masters of Writing.
s0188.idiomatic: His son Liang had talent and learning and rose to hall directorate attendant in the masters of writing.

s0190.literal: Qin Zhijing, styled Silin, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang.
s0190.idiomatic: Qin Zhijing, styled Silin, came from Jiyang in Nanyang.

s0191.literal: His father Shanyu in the Liang era was known for classical learning and reached magistrate of Wuning and Director of the Office of Righteousness.
s0191.idiomatic: His father Shanyu was known in the Liang era for classical learning and rose to magistrate of Wuning and director of the office of righteousness.

s0192.literal: Zhijing at age five read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and kin all sighed in wonder.
s0192.idiomatic: Zhijing at five read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and kin all marveled.

s0193.literal: At sixteen he was examined on the Exegesis of the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and was selected in the top grade.
s0193.idiomatic: At sixteen he was examined on the Zuo Tradition exegesis and the meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and placed in the top grade.

s0194.literal: The Imperial Censor memorialized: "The imperial court has many scholars, but as a rule they stop at understanding the Classics; men like Yan and Min ought to rank in the top grade.
s0194.idiomatic: The imperial censor memorialized, "The court has many scholars who as a rule only pass the classics examination; men like Yan and Min ought to rank at the top."

s0195.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang examined his answers and said: "What harm if I too have a Yan and Min?
s0195.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang read his answers and said, "What harm if I too have a Yan and Min?"

s0196.literal: " He then summoned him for a face-to-face examination, had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered Master of Writing Attendant Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and intone the chapter for scholars, and the Emperor himself debated him.
s0196.idiomatic: He then summoned him for a face-to-face test, had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered master of writing attendant Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and intone the chapter for scholars, and debated him himself.

s0197.literal: Zhijing analyzed and explained freely in all directions and answered like an echo; none left or right failed to sigh in admiration.
s0197.idiomatic: Zhijing analyzed freely in every direction and answered like an echo; none present failed to admire him.

s0198.literal: He was then made Gentleman of the Palace Carriage for Youth and richly rewarded.
s0198.idiomatic: He was then made Gentleman of the Palace Carriage for Youth and richly rewarded.

s0199.literal: At eighteen he attended the Dharma assembly at Chongyun Hall; at the time Emperor Wu personally performed the incense rite, gazed long at Zhijing, and said: "Not long since I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap!
s0199.idiomatic: At eighteen he attended the dharma assembly at Chongyun Hall; Emperor Wu personally performed the incense rite, gazed long at Zhijing, and said, "It seems but yesterday I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap!"

s0200.literal: " That same day he was made Erudite within the Imperial University quota.
s0200.idiomatic: That same day he was made erudite within the imperial university quota.
